QUESTION ONE: MOMENTUM AND CIRCULAR MOTION

Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system. For this question, ignore gravitational effects of other moons and assume Europa is in a perfectly circular orbit.

Mass of Jupiter: 1.90 x 10^27 kg
Radius of Jupiter: 6.99 x 10^7 m
Mass of Europa: 4.80 x 10^22 kg
Distance between centres of mass: 6.71 x 10^8 m

Show that the centre of mass of Jupiter and Europa is 1.70 x 10^4 m from the centre of Jupiter.

Two ice particles around Jupiter move toward each other at right angles. Particle A has mass 3.10 kg and velocity 10.0 m s-1; Particle B has mass 4.50 kg and velocity 12.0 m s-1. They collide and stick together.

Calculate the size and direction of the momentum of the combined particles. State direction relative to initial velocity of particle A.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Individual momenta calculated.

For Merit:
- Total momentum correct.

For Excellence:
- Size and angle correct.

questions.text:
Astronauts on the International Space Station appear weightless, even though Earth's gravity acts on them.

Explain why astronauts appear weightless yet remain in orbit.
questions.expectedAnswer: The gravitational force provides exactly the centripetal force needed for the circular orbit. The astronauts and the station are in free fall together — they accelerate toward Earth at the same rate. There is no contact (normal) force between the astronaut and the station floor, so the astronaut feels weightless. They remain in orbit because their tangential velocity means they continually fall toward Earth but miss it.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- One correct statement.

For Merit:
- Two linked.

For Excellence:
- Full explanation.

questions.text:
QUESTION TWO: ROTATIONAL MOTION

Hana and Wiremu are playing on a roundabout (merry-go-round) of radius 1.40 m. Wiremu stands on it while Hana pushes. Starting from rest, Hana accelerates it so that it takes 10.0 s to make 3.00 rotations.

Show that the angular velocity after 10.0 s is 3.77 rad s-1.
questions.expectedAnswer: theta = 3.00 x 2 pi = 18.85 rad. theta = (omega_f + omega_i)/2 x t. 18.85 = (omega_f/2) x 10.0. omega_f = 3.77 rad s-1.

questions.text:
Later, both stand on the edge while the roundabout rotates at constant angular velocity. Wiremu moves inward.

Explain the effect on the rotational kinetic energy of the system.
questions.expectedAnswer: Angular momentum is conserved (no external torque). As Wiremu moves inward, I decreases (I proportional to mr^2). Since L = I omega is constant, omega increases. E_k_rot = 1/2 I omega^2 = L^2/(2I). Since I decreases and L is constant, E_k_rot increases. The extra energy comes from the work done by Wiremu as he moves inward against the centripetal tendency.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- I decreases OR omega increases.

For Merit:
- Two concepts linked.

For Excellence:
- All four concepts linked.

questions.text:
Hana holds the string and moves her hand horizontally from side to side. At a certain frequency, the ball oscillates with a very large amplitude.

Explain why this occurs. Include force and energy considerations.
questions.expectedAnswer: This is resonance. When the driving frequency matches the natural frequency of the pendulum, energy is transferred most efficiently into the system. The driving force is in phase with the velocity, adding energy each cycle. Friction removes some energy, but at resonance, energy input exceeds loss, so amplitude builds up to a maximum.

WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Resonance or driving force.

For Merit:
- Force or energy explanation.

For Excellence:
- Both force and energy.
